title: Some gym tab tests check rules the app no longer uses, so they pass whatever the screens do
what: Five gym rules are now only called by tests: the gym name in Settings, the check of a typed gym code before joining, the second line of the Ask a trainer row, reading a claim code, and the check-in poster link. The screens use other copies of these rules, so the tests stay green even if the real screen goes wrong.
expected: Each test checks the rule the screen really uses, and a rule no screen uses is removed with its test.
fix_line: Point the tests at the rules the screens use and delete the unused copies

title: Switched-off sample shop and staff sign-in stay in the gym tab code, with unused leftovers
what: The sample shop has no way in, yet its words, its pretend order and a check that always says yes are still kept. The staff sign-in card is switched off but still built. A forget step for Find my gym is never called, though its note says Erase all data uses it.
expected: Code for switched-off parts is removed or clearly parked, and a forget step that Erase all data needs is really called.
fix_line: Remove the sample shop leftovers and check whether Erase all data should forget a found gym

title: The time words (like 5:42 pm) are written out three separate times in the gym tab
what: Ask a trainer, check-in and the shop's prices-as-of line each build the time words with their own copy of the same rule, next to a shared date file that has none of it.
expected: One shared time rule used by all three, so a change reaches every screen.
fix_line: Move the time words into the shared date file and use it in all three places

title: A failed refresh of the gym messages bell leaves no trace
what: When the gym is checked, the bell's messages are refreshed and any crash in that step is thrown away with no log, unlike every other step next to it.
expected: The failure is written to the log like its neighbours.
fix_line: Log the failure instead of dropping it

title: 26 gym tab screens have no test that loads them, and the few screen tests only look for words in the code
what: The bag, pay panels, check-in, messages, membership, plan request and 20 more gym tab files are never loaded by any test. The tests that do touch the gym tab screens read the code as text and look for words, so a screen that crashes or shows the wrong thing still passes.
expected: The money and check-in screens at least are drawn in a test and their buttons pressed.
fix_line: Add drawn-screen tests for the pay, bag and check-in screens first

title: A leave-the-gym test fails if the test machine is slow
what: One test checks that the app does not wait on an unanswered leave by racing the gym check against a real 200 millisecond timer. On a busy cloud machine the check can take longer and the test fails with nothing wrong.
expected: The test uses a pretend clock or checks the order of steps, not real time.
how_often: now and then on slow test runs
fix_line: Use a pretend clock in that test
